title: Latent Memory Palace: Reasoning for Control as Autoregressive Variational Inference
hook: LLMs can choose to think longer on hard questions. This paper gets robot control policies to do the same — allocating adaptive test-time compute in a latent 'memory palace' instead of language.
key_points: Language-space reasoning doesn't transfer well to continuous control: it lacks the spatial granularity needed for precise motions.
Latent Memory Palace (LMP) reframes control-time reasoning as variational inference over an autoregressive latent space, with iterative, adaptive retrieval — not language tokens.
Derives a latent-space RL technique to directly optimize the resulting variational lower bound.
The resulting policy, LMP-π, performs strongly in both simulation and real-world robot tasks.
Test-time compute allocation is interpretable and adaptive — the policy 'deliberates' more on harder decisions.
The same framework also yields a variable-length action tokenizer (LMP-tok) that improves other downstream autoregressive policies.
content_html: Language models can choose to reason longer on hard questions and answer quickly on easy ones. Robot control policies mostly can't — reasoning in language space doesn't have the spatial precision continuous control needs. Latent Memory Palace, from a University of Washington robotics/RL group, builds that adaptive deliberation directly into a control policy's latent space instead.
extra_html:
LMP treats control-time reasoning as variational inference over an autoregressive latent space — organizing information the way a "memory palace" does, with retrieval that's iterative and adapts to the situation rather than fixed. The authors derive a latent-space reinforcement learning technique to tractably optimize the resulting variational lower bound, producing a policy called LMP-π that performs strongly across both simulated and real-world control tasks while allocating test-time compute in an interpretable, adaptive way — more "deliberation" on harder decisions, less on easy ones.

The same underlying framework also produces a variable-length action tokenizer, LMP-tok, which the authors show improves other downstream autoregressive policies that use it. The paper's broader claim is a new way to think about latent reasoning for control: not as a language-space add-on, but as variational inference native to the control problem itself. Chuning Zhu, Abhishek Gupta, and colleagues, arXiv 2026.

related.title: DreamerV3: Mastering Domains through World Models
related.hook: Instead of learning only from real experience, DreamerV3 builds a world model and practices inside its own imagination — one fixed config, 150+ tasks.

related.title: π0: A Vision-Language-Action Model
related.hook: π0 is a generalist robot policy: it takes camera images, joint angles, and a plain-language instruction, and outputs smooth action sequences — folding laundry, bussing tables, bagging groceries.

related.title: World Models Meet Language Models
related.hook: A world model can imagine what happens next; an LLM can reason about it. The hard part is knowing when to trust the daydream — and when the simulation is just plausible nonsense.

flashcards.prompt: Why doesn't language-space reasoning transfer well to continuous control policies?
flashcards.back_html: It lacks the spatial granularity needed for precise, fine-grained motions — control needs more than what discrete language tokens can represent.

flashcards.prompt: How does Latent Memory Palace (LMP) formulate control-time reasoning?

choices.text: As variational inference over an autoregressive latent space, with iterative adaptive retrieval
As a chain-of-thought reasoning trace written in natural language
As a fixed lookup table of precomputed actions

flashcards.explanation_html: LMP treats reasoning as variational inference with an autoregressive latent distribution, optimized via a derived latent-space RL technique — not language-based chain-of-thought.

flashcards.prompt: Besides the LMP-π policy, what other reusable output does the framework produce?
flashcards.back_html: A variable-length action tokenizer, LMP-tok, which the authors show improves downstream autoregressive control policies that adopt it.
